note: 10 pages total (9 content pages + home), organised under a 6-item main nav — Home, About, Programs, Impact, Our Jamii, Contact. This is a deliberate IA consolidation from the original 21-page inventory (see docs/content-seeding-plan.md §2 for the historical breakdown), carried out to remove duplicate hero headers, duplicate CTA bands and a 5-group dropdown mega-nav that fragmented closely related content across too many thin pages. 'about' absorbed the former 'problem' and 'careers' pages as in-page subsections; 'programs' absorbed 'results', 'register', 'requirements', 'calendar' and 'findus'; 'partnerships' absorbed 'partner', 'government', 'finance', 'donors' and 'corporate'; 'impact' absorbed 'stories' and 'reports'; 'form' was renamed to 'apply' unchanged in substance. 'news-events' was split back out of 'impact' on a follow-up request — it absorbed the former 'latest' and 'events' pages, which had briefly lived as anchored sections on 'impact' during the first consolidation pass. 'team' was added later still (2026-08-16), reached via About's submenu like 'partnerships' — a dedicated staff/board page, not folded into 'about' as a section, since it's an org-chart-shaped list that will keep growing/changing on its own schedule, unrelated to 'about's narrative content. 'our-jamii' was added the same day as its own top-level nav item (not a submenu page like 'team'/'partnerships') — it introduces the communities CECF serves (MSMEs, women's groups, youth, gender/GBV support, vulnerable communities, refugees, persons with disabilities, older persons) and links out to apps/jamii, the separate community-pages platform in this monorepo (see App\Support\PageUrl::jamiiUrl()/JAMII_URL), so it's a distinct top-level concept — not a section of 'about' or 'impact' — with its own audience-facing CTAs (browse community pages, start a page, register with CECF). 'partnerships', 'apply', 'news-events' and 'team' are the pages judged too distinct to fold further into their parent as plain sections — partnerships is a five-audience institutional-relations page, apply is a transactional multi-step form, news-events is fast-changing/dated content that would otherwise sit awkwardly next to impact's mostly-static annual narrative, and team is a people list — each is kept as its own page, reached only via a submenu (see ../navigation.json: About > Partnerships / Our team, Programs > Register / Apply, Impact > News & events) and via in-page CTAs, not as flat top-level nav items. 'slug' is this plan's recommended real WordPress permalink slug, replacing the template's '#/<key>' hash route — see content-seeding-plan.md decision #2. 'key' is stable and matches the filename in pages/<key>.json and the template's original route id, so it survives if the slug is renamed later.
